issues.description: raise PerformanceWarning(...) misuses a Warning class as an exception, with misleading name vs data-loss semantics
issues.detail: The code does `raise PerformanceWarning(msg)` to abort the write. If dask's PerformanceWarning subclasses `Warning` (the conventional pattern), raising it works but is semantically wrong: warnings are meant for `warnings.warn`, and the name signals 'slow' rather than 'will lose data'. The error message itself says 'To avoid risk of data loss', which is a correctness concern, not a performance one. Either use `warnings.warn(..., PerformanceWarning)` (and accept the misalignment behavior the author wanted to prevent) or raise a real exception subclass (e.g., ValueError) with a clear name. The current shape will confuse users and any `warnings.filterwarnings` rules they have set.

Inside the `for ax, ...` loop the code does `raise PerformanceWarning(msg)` immediately followed by `break`. `raise` unwinds the stack, so the `break` is unreachable. This is a smell that the author intended to collect or report multiple axes but only the first failure is reported. Decide: either iterate and accumulate all misaligned axes into one message, or remove the dead `break` and document that only the first failing axis is shown.

issues.description: Only checks dw[0]; non-uniform chunk tuples from auto_chunks are not validated
issues.detail: `normalize_chunks(chunks='auto', ...)` returns a tuple of per-axis chunk-size tuples that can be non-uniform (e.g., last chunk smaller). The check uses only `dw[0]` as the 'nominal' size. If auto_chunks ever returns interior chunks of different sizes (rare but possible for certain shapes), or if dw[0] happens to be aligned while another interior block is not, the check is wrong. Iterate all entries except the trailing remainder (or assert that all interior chunks are equal multiples of `zw`).

issues.description: safe_chunk_size computes product of all shard dims, but only the current axis is misaligned
issues.detail: `safe_chunk_size = np.prod(zarr_write_chunks) * max(1, z.dtype.itemsize)` computes the total bytes of a full shard across every axis. For high-dimensional arrays this can vastly overstate the minimum `array.chunk-size` the user needs to set to make this particular axis safe. The recommendation should be the smallest value that makes auto_chunks produce a multiple of `zw` on the offending axis. As written, a user following the suggested config value may receive larger chunks than necessary across every other axis.

issues.description: `if not nominal_dask_chunk_size % zw == 0` is fragile due to operator precedence
issues.detail: Python parses this as `not (nominal_dask_chunk_size % zw == 0)`, which is what the author wants — but it reads as `(not nominal_dask_chunk_size % zw) == 0`, and the next reader will pause. Replace with the obviously-correct `if nominal_dask_chunk_size % zw != 0:`.

issues.description: No test coverage for the raise path when region is specified
issues.detail: The new parametrized happy-path test covers `region in {None, 'all', 'half'}`, but `test_zarr_risky_shards_warns` only exercises `region=None`. The misalignment check sits before the `if region is None` split, so the same code path runs for the region case — but there is no test to confirm it. Add a parametrization over region to the warning test, or at least one explicit region case.

issues.description: PR description explicitly raises an unresolved design question that should be answered before merge
issues.detail: The author asks 'What should we do when there's competition between the global config and shard shape? Would an exception be appropriate here?' and then ships the exception. This is a real API/UX decision: silently override the user's `array.chunk-size` config to keep them safe, vs hard-fail and force them to opt in. Either option is defensible, but the diff lands one without a maintainer-level signoff visible in the description. Lock the answer (and document it in the error message and changelog) before merging.
`numpy.dtype.itemsize` is always >= 1 for real dtypes. The `max(1, ...)` adds no safety and invites the reader to wonder which dtype has itemsize 0. Drop the max.

issues.description: `np.prod(...)` returns a numpy scalar that may render oddly in the error message
issues.detail: `np.prod` returns a numpy integer (e.g., `np.int64`). Depending on numpy version this may format as `np.int64(12)` inside the example `dask.config.set({...})` snippet, which would suggest invalid Python to the user. Cast with `int(...)` before interpolation, and consider using `math.prod` for clarity.

issues.description: Error message punctuation: 'at least the size in bytes of a single on-disk chunk (or shard)' is wordy and slightly ambiguous
issues.detail: Suggest tightening to 'at least the on-disk shard size in bytes ({safe_chunk_size}); e.g. dask.config.set({"array.chunk-size": {safe_chunk_size}})'. Avoids the 'chunk (or shard)' parenthetical that may confuse users who already separate the two concepts.

issues.description: Renamed test loosens its assertion from exact chunk equality to divisibility
issues.detail: The previous test asserted `result.chunks == ((zarr_shard_shape[0], zarr_shard_shape[0]),)`. The new test only checks `all(c % s == 0 for c, s in zip(result.chunksize, zarr_shard_shape))`. That is appropriate for the new 'multiple of shard shape' behavior, but consider also asserting that the resulting chunk size is `>= zarr_shard_shape[i]` and ideally close to the auto-chunk target, so the test catches regressions where rechunking degenerates to per-shard chunks.

issues.description: `zarr_write_chunks` is recomputed once at top-level — good — but `dask_write_chunks` is now used for the region branch's chunk-derivation in place of the previous `normalize_chunks(write_chunks, z.shape)`
issues.detail: In the old code, `old_chunks = normalize_chunks(write_chunks, z.shape)` was passed into `new_blockdim`. The new code passes `dask_write_chunks` (the auto-chunked tuple). For region writes, the chunks must still tile the *region*, not the full array, after intersection with the index. The `new_blockdim` call is supposed to handle that, but the semantics change from 'shard-sized chunks tiling z.shape' to 'auto-sized multiples of shards tiling z.shape', which could yield larger-than-expected blocks within a small region. Worth a focused test covering a small region against an array with very large auto-chunks.

dissents.topic: Raise an exception vs warn-and-rechunk-anyway when config conflicts with shard shape

positions.position: Hard-fail is right. Silently overriding user config to write shard-misaligned data risks data loss; an exception forces an informed decision and is the only safe default.

Warn loudly via warnings.warn(PerformanceWarning) and still write safely by rounding up to the shard size. Raising on a value the user already set globally will break pipelines on upgrade; the library should fix it for them and tell them about it.

Don't raise a class named PerformanceWarning. Either issue it as a warning or rename to ZarrShardAlignmentError / ValueError. The current shape will be cited as anti-pattern in linters and confuse downstream `warnings.filterwarnings` users.
PerformanceWarning is already exported from dask.array.core and may be load-bearing elsewhere; reusing it minimizes API surface churn. Document the dual use in the docstring and move on.
Check every interior chunk on every axis, not just dw[0]. auto_chunks is allowed to produce non-uniform tuples; one wrong block can corrupt one shard.
auto_chunks in practice returns uniform interior chunks plus a remainder. Checking dw[0] covers the realistic cases and keeps the diff small. Add a comment instead of a loop.

review.summary: The change is the right direction — using shard shape as `previous_chunks` so `auto_chunks` produces shard-aligned multiples is a meaningful improvement over #12105. But the implementation ships two clear bugs that should block merge: a dead `break` after an unconditional `raise`, and the misuse of a class named `PerformanceWarning` as a hard exception for what the message itself calls a 'data loss' condition. Several P1 issues remain around only checking `dw[0]`, over-estimating `safe_chunk_size` by multiplying all shard dims, fragile operator-precedence in the divisibility check, and missing test coverage for the region-write path of the raise. The PR description itself flags an unresolved design question (raise vs warn-and-fix) that should be settled by a maintainer before this lands. Nits on `max(1, itemsize)`, `np.prod` returning a numpy scalar inside the user-facing config example, and a loosened test assertion are easy cleanups.
